data.title: The group chats that changed America
data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了美国政治中通过加密群聊（如Signal和WhatsApp）进行的幕后讨论如何影响公众舆论和政治结盟。这些私人聊天始于新冠疫情期间，参与者包括科技界领袖、风险投资人及政界人士，如Palantir联合创始人Joe Lonsdale和前Coinbase首席技术官Balaji Srinivasan。这些讨论不仅涉及政治，还促成了硅谷与美国右翼的结盟，特别是在对特朗普的支持上起到了关键作用。群聊内容通过社交媒体、播客和新闻影响主流观点，成为政治和媒体的“暗物质”。尽管这些讨论通常保密，但其影响日益显著，改变了美国的政治风向。科技右翼的群聊尤其具有影响力，而反特朗普的自由派也在利用类似方式协调立场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过Signal群聊等私人聊天工具，科技精英和政客之间的联系、思想交流及其影响，以及这些聊天曝光的伦理和后果。

不同观点：
• [cloverich] 提出一个项目设想，通过分析政客和智库的言论，生成谁可能在私下交流的图谱，甚至可以展示聊天名称、涉及思想和时间线。该观点侧重于技术实现和信息可视化。

• [cptroot] 和 [pbiggar] 等人引用Chris Rufo的例子，指出科技精英通过群聊影响政治和意识形态，尤其是像Chesa Boudin召回运动这样的政治活动。这表明群聊不仅仅是社交工具，而是具有实际政治影响力的组织手段。

• [hsuduebc2] 认为，科技精英由于一系列丑闻（如Cambridge Analytica事件），失去了公众信任，但他们没有反思自己的行为，反而将批评视为意识形态攻击，表现出认知失调。这解释了科技精英为何转向右翼政治。

• [ajross] 补充，许多科技领袖如Andreesen和Musk突然转向右翼，特别是特朗普主义，这种转变并非单纯因为被左派排斥，而是出于一种政治重新定位。

• [doom2] 指出，Hacker News等平台不愿深入讨论硅谷人物转向右翼的原因，并质疑为何保守派在建立意识形态同质空间时没有受到类似左派的批评。

• [mindslight] 认为，尽管自己支持公开辩论并反对取消文化，但通过这些群聊释放出来的政治力量证明了公众对科技精英言论的负面反应是有道理的。该评论还探讨了精英犹太阴谋论等极端思想，并提出如何应对这些思想的社会讨论。

• [freshfunk] 对私人聊天泄露表示反感，认为这破坏了信任和开放交流，导致人们更不愿参与公开对话，最终限制了思想的多样性和全球视野。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还提到了具体群聊影响力的实例链接，如[pbiggar]分享的关于亲以色列信息和商业领袖的文章，进一步支持了群聊具有广泛政治影响的观点。
• [blitzar] 和 [philipwhiuk] 将Signal群聊比作新的"俱乐部"和"沼泽"，暗示这些私下交流已经成为权力运作的核心。

争议焦点：
• 科技精英群聊的政治影响以及他们转向右翼的真实原因。
• 私人聊天泄露的伦理问题，以及这种行为对公开辩论和社会信任的损害。
• 保守派在建立同质意识形态空间时是否应受到与左派相同的批评。

The Scoop
Last Thursday morning, a bit before 10 am in Austin and nearly 11 pm in Singapore, Joe Lonsdale had enough of Balaji Srinivasanâs views on China.
âThis is insane CCP thinking,â Lonsdale, a co-founder of Palantir, wrote to a 300-member Signal group. âNot sure what leaders hang out w you in Singapore but on this you have been taken over by a crazy China mind virus.â
Srinivasan, a former Coinbase chief technology officer and influential tech figure who now lives in the city-state, responded that China âexecuted extremely well over 45 years. Any analysis that doesnât take that into account makes it seem like the US could have held it back.â
AD
It was a normal, robust disagreement among friends in a friendly space (as
both
raced
to X to declare, after I emailed them about it).
And it was just another day in Chatham House, a giant and raucous Signal group that forms part of the sprawling network of influential private chats that began during the fervid early days of the COVID-19 pandemic, and which have fueled a new alliance of tech and the US right. That same week in Chatham House, Lonsdale and the Democratic billionaire Mark Cuban sparred over affirmative action, and Cuban and Daily Wire founder Ben Shapiro discussed questions of culture and work ethic.
This constellation of rolling elite political conversations revolve primarily around the venture capitalist Marc Andreessen and a circle of Silicon Valley figures. None of their participants was surprised to see Trump administration officials
firing off
secrets and emojis on the platform last month. I did not have the good fortune to be accidentally added to one of the chats, which can be set to make messages disappear after just 30 seconds.
But their influence flows through X, Substack, and podcasts, and constitutes a kind of dark matter of American politics and media. The group chats arenât always primarily a political space,Â but they are the single most important place in which a stunning realignment toward Donald Trump was shaped and negotiated, and an alliance between Silicon Valley and the new right formed. The group chats are âthe memetic upstream of mainstream opinion,â wrote one of their key organizers, Sriram Krishnan, a former partner in the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (typically styled a16z) who is now the White House senior policy adviser for AI.
AD
Of course, these are hardly the only power group chats. Anti-Trump liberals are now coordinating their responses on Signal. There are group chats for Black political elites and morning show producers. A vast and influential parallel set of tech conversations take place on WhatsApp. Thereâs a big China-friendly group over on WeChat. Elite podcasters have one.
âItâs the same thing happening on both sides, and Iâve been amazed at how much this is coordinating our reality,â said the writer Thomas Chatterton Williams, who was for a time a member of a group chat with Andreessen. âIf you werenât in the business at all, youâd think everyone was arriving at conclusions independently âÂ and [theyâre] not. Itâs a small group of people who talk to each other and overlap between politics and journalism and a few industries.â
But there is no equivalent to the intellectual counterculture that grew up over the last five years on the tech right, and no figure remotely like Andreessen, the towering, enthusiastic 53-year old who co-founded a16z and, before that, invented the modern web browser.
AD
In February, he
described
the group chats to the podcaster Lex Fridman as âthe equivalent of samizdatâ â the self-published Soviet underground press âÂ in a âsoft authoritarianâ age of social media shaming and censorship. âThe combination of encryption and disappearing messages really unleashed it,â he said. The chats, he
wrote
recently, helped produce our national âvibe shift.â
The chats are occasionally marked by the sort of thing that would have gotten you scolded on Twitter in 2020, and which would pass unremarked-on on X in 2025.
They have rarely been discussed in public, though you can catch the occasional mention in, for instance, a
podcast debate
between Cuban and the Republican entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy, which started in a chat.
But they are made visible through a group consensus on social media. Their effects have ranged from the mainstreaming of the monarchist pundit Curtis Yarvin to a particularly focused and developed dislike of the former Washington Post writer Taylor Lorenz.

data.title: Naur's "Programming as Theory Building" and LLMs replacing human programmers
data.author: bertman
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLM）是否能替代人类程序员的工作，并引用了Naur的论文来论证LLM无法建立“理论”，而理论是编程工作的核心。文章引用了哲学家Gilbert Ryle的“理论”概念，指出理论是程序员在实际工作中逐步建立的，而不是简单地从代码或文档中获取。LLM虽然可以生成看似有理论支持的代码，但它们只是“消化”已有工作成果，并不能真正建立理论。编程不仅仅是生成文本，而是构建和维护对程序的理解。文章强调，只有通过实际参与项目，才能获得对大型程序的理论理解，这是LLM无法实现的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）是否能够进行理论构建和取代程序员的工作

不同观点：
• n4r9认为，LLM目前的表现只是一种 illusion（幻觉），它们并没有真正构建理论。他指出，要证明LLM的理论构建能力是幻觉，也需要解释人类看似拥有理论时是否同样为幻觉。此外，n4r9还认为，理论是通过实际工作发展出来的，而LLM并没有真正进行这些工作。
• andriesm 则认为，LLM确实能够进行一定程度的推理和理论构建，尽管目前能力有限，但它们在解决编码问题和记忆理论方面已经非常有用。通过适当的提示和描述，可以提高LLM在大型代码库中的表现。
• ebiester 持相对乐观的态度，认为虽然目前LLM不能完全取代程序员，但技术在进步，未来可能通过结合更大的上下文窗口和其他技术来模拟程序员的理论构建能力。
• falcor84 反驳了对LLM不能构建理论的批评，认为通过bootstrapping（自举），AI可以在工作过程中逐步构建理论。
• andai 指出，LLM在处理自己设计的系统时表现更好，因为这些系统符合其自身的“期望”和“习惯”。
• woah 批评关于LLM不能做什么的哲学性争论，认为这些争论往往在几个月内就被证明是错误的，主张让实验结果来说明问题。
• BenoitEssiambre 引用Solomonoff归纳理论，认为LLM在尝试进行理论构建，并指出OpenAI的研究者正在朝这个方向努力。
• philipswood 认为，LLM在预测工作结果的过程中，可能通过某种逆向工程“进行工作”，并指出讨论应避免以人类为中心的“推理”和“意识”定义。
• BiraIgnacio 认为，尽管LLM不应该能够取代程序员，但它们有可能做到这一点。
• analyte123 指出，LLM在缺乏上下文信息时表现不足，强调变量类型和模式定义的重要性。
• xpe 认为，LLM可以通过“思考链”和补充文档来“进行工作”，并强调应通过实验结果来评价LLM的能力，而不是通过其内部机制是否与人类相似。
• edanm 批评那些长篇大论却容易被事实推翻的文章，认为这是无意义的争论。
• IanCal 认为文章中引用的权威论据是逻辑谬误，质疑文章的有效性。
• fedeb95 指出，LLM目前缺乏“为什么”做某事的理由，即缺乏目的性，这是一个比技术更根本的难题。

补充讨论：
• LLM是否能够进行理论构建和工作是一个核心争议点，涉及到LLM的内在机制、实际表现和未来潜力。
• 讨论中多次提到应通过实验和实际结果来评价LLM的能力，而不是单纯依赖理论推导。
• 关于LLM是否能够取代程序员，存在乐观和悲观两种态度，乐观者认为技术在进步，而悲观者则关注LLM的当前局限性。
• 关于“为什么”做某事（目的性）的讨论，指出这是当前LLM和其他技术面临的一个深层次问题。

43818169.article_content:
For a copy of Naur’s paper and also my notes about it,
see:
Dave’s Paper Notes: Programming as Theory Building
In this essay, I will perform the logical fallacy of
argument from authority
(wikipedia.org) to attack the notion
that large language model (LLM)-based generative "AI"
systems are capable of doing the work of human
programmers.
LLMs have no "theory"
To understand Naur’s paper, you need to understand what
he means by "theory", which comes from
philosopher Gilbert Ryle’s
The Concept of Mind
(wikipedia.org).
The Wikipedia page I linked above is not a great place to
learn this term and Naur’s use. Instead here’s an analogy by
Ryle in the form of a rather long paragraph from The Concept
of the Mind (Chapter IX The Intellect), starting on page
263:
"If a farmer has made a path, he is able to saunter easily up
and down it.  That is what the path was made for. But the
work of making the path was not a process of sauntering
easily, but one of marking the ground, digging, fetching
loads of gravel, rolling and draining. He dug and rolled
where there was yet no path, so that he might in the end
have a path on which he could
saunter without any more digging or rolling. Similarly a
person who has a theory can, among other things, expound to
himself, or the world, the whole theory or any part of it;
he can, so to speak, saunter in prose from any part to any
other part of it. But the work of building the theory was a
job of making paths where as yet there were none. The point
of the analogy is this. Epistemologists very frequently
describe the labours of building theories in terms
appropriate only to the business of going over or teaching a
theory that one already has; as if, for example, the chains
of propositions which constitute Euclid’s 'Elements'
mirrored a parallel succession of theorising moves made by
Euclid in his original labours of making his geometrical
discoveries; as if, that is, what Euclid was equipped to do
when he had his theory, he was already equipped to do when
constructing it. But this is absurd. On the other hand,
epistemologists sometimes tell the opposite story,
describing what Euclid did in delivering his theories when
he had them, as if it was some recrudescence of the original
theorising work. This, too, is absurd. These epistemologists
describe using a path, as if it were a piece of path-making;
the others describe the path-making, as if it were a piece
of path-using."
One must not confuse the artifact with the mind that
produced that artifact.
I think something that clouds the whole business is that
LLMs are capable of
appearing
to have a theory about a
program. From Naur’s paper:
"…​theory is understood as the knowledge a person must have in order not only to do certain things intelligently but also to explain them, to answer queries about them, to argue about them, and so forth."
Indeed LLMs might seem to have this ability, but it’s,
charitably, illusion. The appearance of a thing is not the
thing.  An LLM cannot obtain a Ryleian "theory" because,
well, that’s impossible. LLMs "train" on bodies of work.  By
Ryle’s definition, the text output of theory-making can
never be the theory itself.
Theories are developed by
doing the work
and LLMs do not
do the work. They ingest the output of work.
Theory building doesn’t work backwards like that. In fact,
that’s Naur’s whole point with this paper:
First, you cannot obtain the "theory" of a large program
without actually working with that program. Reading the
source or even documentation cannot, by some magical
transference, give you the same mind that produced the
program in the first place.
Second, you cannot
effectively
work on a large program
without a working "theory" of that program.
Naur explains:
"The conclusion seems inescapable that at least with certain kinds of large programs, the continued adaption, modification, and correction of errors in them, is essentially dependent on a certain kind of knowledge possessed by a group of programmers who are closely and continuously connected with them."
Neither machine code nor source code contain the wisdom of
knowing
how
the program works. Nor does it contain the
wisdom to know
why
the program was written the way it was
instead of some other way that would have accomplished the
same task.
Programming is not text production
This is my favorite part of Naur’s paper because it is so
practical and visceral. It builds on the "theory" part, but
also stands on it’s own.
Writing software is the production of code in the same way
that writing poetry is the production of words. In both
cases, the code and the words are the artifacts of the real
work: building and maintaining a theory of the program.
As Naur writes:
"…​it is important to have an appropriate understanding of what programming is. If our understanding is inappropriate we will misunderstand the difficulties that arise in the activity and our attempts to overcome them will give rise to conflicts and frustrations."

• andai 指出，LLM在处理自己设计的系统时表现更好，因为这些系统符合其自身的“期望”和“习惯”。
• woah 批评关于LLM不能做什么的哲学性争论，认为这些争论往往在几个月内就被证明是错误的，主张让实验结果来说明问题。
• BenoitEssiambre 引用Solomonoff归纳理论，认为LLM在尝试进行理论构建，并指出OpenAI的研究者正在朝这个方向努力。
• philipswood 认为，LLM在预测工作结果的过程中，可能通过某种逆向工程“进行工作”，并指出讨论应避免以人类为中心的“推理”和“意识”定义。
• BiraIgnacio 认为，尽管LLM不应该能够取代程序员，但它们有可能做到这一点。
• analyte123 指出，LLM在缺乏上下文信息时表现不足，强调变量类型和模式定义的重要性。
• xpe 认为，LLM可以通过“思考链”和补充文档来“进行工作”，并强调应通过实验结果来评价LLM的能力，而不是通过其内部机制是否与人类相似。
• edanm 批评那些长篇大论却容易被事实推翻的文章，认为这是无意义的争论。
• IanCal 认为文章中引用的权威论据是逻辑谬误，质疑文章的有效性。
• fedeb95 指出，LLM目前缺乏“为什么”做某事的理由，即缺乏目的性，这是一个比技术更根本的难题。

补充讨论：
• LLM是否能够进行理论构建和工作是一个核心争议点，涉及到LLM的内在机制、实际表现和未来潜力。
• 讨论中多次提到应通过实验和实际结果来评价LLM的能力，而不是单纯依赖理论推导。
• 关于LLM是否能够取代程序员，存在乐观和悲观两种态度，乐观者认为技术在进步，而悲观者则关注LLM的当前局限性。
• 关于“为什么”做某事（目的性）的讨论，指出这是当前LLM和其他技术面临的一个深层次问题。

data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了中国在临床试验方面的快速增长。2017年，中国启动的临床试验仅有600多项，而到2023年，这一数字已接近2000。文章指出，中国政府通过一系列政策改革，如优先审查、有条件批准以及“默示许可”政策，加快了新药临床试验的审批速度。此外，中国加入国际人用药品注册技术协调会（ICH）后，接受海外临床试验数据，减少了在国内重复试验的需求。这些改革吸引了国际投资，推动了中国生物技术行业的繁荣。相比之下，美国的临床试验数量在2010年代末趋于稳定，而中国则迅速赶上。文章最后建议，美国可以借鉴中国的经验，以加速药物开发过程。

In 2017, there were just over 600 clinical trials initiated in China. By 2023, that number was nearly 2,000. How can American companies kick off a similar boom?
Hiya Jain

In January, the Chinese company Deepseek released a reasoning AI model, called R1, that
performs comparably
to OpenAI's GPT-4o Turbo model on certain AI benchmarks but was developed with fewer resources at a much lower cost. Marc Andreessen called it “one of the most amazing and impressive breakthroughs I’ve ever seen,” even as NVIDIA’s stock plummeted by 17 percent — the largest ever one-day loss for a U.S. company.
While China’s AI competitiveness may have blindsided the tech world, the
pharmaceutical industry
has already had quite a few “
DeepSeek Moments
” of its own.
About
one-fourth of all clinical trials
and early drug development now happens in China. Large pharmaceutical companies in-license about a third of their experimental molecules from Chinese laboratories (meaning they purchase the rights to molecules developed by other research groups rather than discover them in-house), according to
a report
by Stifel. Just a couple of years ago, this number was about 10 percent.
"Ten years ago, a major [pharmaceutical company] seeking their next breakthrough molecule would have turned to an American or European biotech,” writes biotechnologist
Alex Telford
. “Today, they’re just as likely to license a molecule from a Chinese company. Chinese companies will often run the phase I trial in China for cheap, then flip it to a Western [pharmaceutical company] to run the expensive US trials and bring the drug to market."
The reason for this shift is due, in part, to policy. Chinese regulators have passed reforms that lower barriers to market entry and streamline approvals. Those reforms could hold lessons for U.S. regulators hoping to speed up drug development, too.
Sign up for Asimov Press. It will always be free.
Subscribe
Impacts from China’s reforms can be seen by looking at clinical trial enrollment data.
1
Such data is illuminating because enrollment numbers offer a measure of the administrative burden placed on new treatments as they move from concept to real-world testing. Patent filings and R&D budgets suggest how much a region invests in discovery, but clinical trial activity shows how projects navigate bureaucratic landscapes. By analyzing how enrollment rates respond to changes in policy, funding, and disease targets, we can see which approaches most effectively accelerate pharmaceutical innovation. Here’s what the data shows.
In the early 2010s, the number of clinical trials performed by American companies increased steadily but then leveled out at about 1,900 studies each year. China’s clinical trial numbers, on the other hand, remained relatively low until the mid-2010s. After the government
streamlined approval policies
, though, the number of clinical trials soared. Chinese companies matched the American clinical trial volume in the span of a few years while sustaining their average enrollment trajectory (at a marginally higher rate).
China’s jump in clinical trial enrollments doesn’t stem from a small number of large, late-phase trials (which would skew the mean), either. Rather, the
number of
original
,
new
drugs
originating in China has
climbed
from almost zero in 2010 to a figure, in 2023, that approaches American totals.
How did they do it?
Chinese regulators introduced several measures to speed up clinical trial approvals, including priority review and conditional approvals for new drugs. Drugs that qualify for priority review often address a critical, unmet clinical need, allowing them to go through an accelerated evaluation timeline.
In 2017, the NMPA (China’s drug regulator) also launched an “implied license” policy, which automatically authorizes a clinical trial if regulators voice no objections within 60 days. That same year, China joined the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) and updated its rules to accept overseas clinical trial data, reducing the need to repeat entire studies within China. This means that companies no longer need to repeat full trials in China if high-quality foreign results exist. Amgen’s
XGEVA
, a medication used to treat bone cancer, was approved in 2019 without further testing requirements based on a global Phase 2 study that included no clinical trial sites in China. Easier approvals and commercially viable results in multiple markets also led to
international investment
, which furthered the country’s biotech boom.

data.title: My takeaways from DjangoCon EU 2025
data.author: SCUSKU
data.article_summary:
DjangoCon EU 2025 在都柏林举行，重点讨论了多个技术主题和最佳实践。数据库方面，讨论了如何使用 `select_for_update` 锁定数据库行以确保并发环境下的数据一致性，建议尽快使用 BigInt 或 UUID 作为主键，并介绍了通过 `PostgresPartitionedModel` 进行数据库表分区以提高性能。此外，还提到通过条件索引大幅减少 PostgreSQL 索引大小，以及使用 `django-postgres-extra` 等工具优化数据库操作。

在性能测试方面，强调编写性能测试以检测视图执行时间，并建议对比本地和云服务器的IO速度以找出瓶颈。还讨论了使用 `strace` 等工具进行系统调用检查，以及通过 `django-neopolitan` 和 `django-auto-prefetch` 等库减少数据库查询。

最佳实践包括在PR中审查SQL迁移文件，计算测试中的数据库查询数量，以及清理旧的功能标志。社区方面，介绍了Django Admin的高度定制案例和用Rust编写的Django模板后端。总体而言，会议展示了Django社区的创新和实用解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Django与HTMX的使用及其相关工具和技术的优缺点

不同观点：
• [seanwilson] 认为HTMX与Django结合可以快速实现功能，但在进行用户点击等交互的UI测试时，需要使用Playwright等工具，而这会使测试变得沉重、缓慢且不稳定。此外，HTMX引入了许多边界情况，如错误处理、显示加载进度以及确保部分更新时页面数据的一致性。相比之下，传统的Django全页面刷新方式避免了这些问题。

• [gitroom] 表示尽管有许多新框架，仍然喜欢使用Django，尤其是在处理混乱的项目时，Django让人想回归使用。

• [fidotron] 质疑现在是否还有很多人选择Django用于新项目。

• [tmnvix] 分享了一个实际案例，通过与演讲者的交流解决了嵌套模态和表单中创建新对象后更新小部件的问题，这个问题已经困扰了他8个月。

• [benwilber0] 讨论了主键的选择，主张使用BigInt而不是UUID。他认为UUID比BigInt大两倍，会无谓地膨胀表和索引，不建议使用UUID作为主键。

• [flakiness] 询问HTMX在Django社区中流行的背景原因，表示自己刚选择Django作为业余项目，对Web开发趋势了解不多。

• [neural_embed] 对会议视频感兴趣，询问是否有YouTube视频链接，但表示未能找到相关视频。

补充讨论：
• HTMX在Django社区的流行背景以及具体应用案例（如嵌套模态和表单更新问题）是值得注意的讨论点。
• 关于主键选择的争论，特别是BigInt与UUID的优劣，是一个技术细节上的争议焦点。
• 对Django在现代Web开发中的使用趋势存在不同看法，有人质疑其在新项目中的使用频率，而有人则因其实用性而回归使用。

争议焦点：
• 使用HTMX是否会引入过多复杂性，特别是在处理部分页面更新时的边界情况。
• 使用BigInt还是UUID作为主键的争议，涉及数据库性能和存储效率。

这些观点展示了Django与HTMX在实际应用中的优缺点，以及开发者在技术选择上的不同考量。

Takeaways from DjangoCon EU 2025
tl;dr:
Dublin and the Django community are awesome.
Zach Bellay published on
April 26, 2025
12 min,
2212 words
Here are some of the most interesting things I learned at DjangoCon EU 2025 in Dublin, Ireland, partially written with the help of AI:
link to talks
My list of the best talks are at the bottom.
Me at DjangoCon EU 2025!
Database
How to lock DB rows from Django
:
select_for_update
locks a row prior to making changes, ensuring data consistency in concurrent environments.
Move to BigInt Primary Keys ASAP
: Always use a BigInt (64 bits) or UUID for primary keys. If your table is nearing 2.1 billion entries (the 32-bit integer limit), you can use negative values to double the range, but this comes with caveats.
Talk
Partition DB Tables by Tenant
: The
PostgresPartitionedModel
mixin helps partition data into separate PostgreSQL partitions based on a value, improving performance for large tables.
see
django-postgres-extra
package for more details
Github
Save 99.8% on space in Postgres Indexes
: Always explicitly set
db_index
on foreign keys. By default, foreign keys are indexed, but you can optimize further:
PostgreSQL builds indexes for null values, but you can add a condition to an
Index
to dramatically reduce index size (up to ~99% smaller).

Write Performance Tests in Pytest
: Write tests that load data into the DB and time how long views take to ensure good performance (or see regressions).
Check Laptop vs Cloud Server IO Speed
: If your DB/app is slower in the cloud, compare cloud disk speed with your laptop's disk speed to see if the bottleneck is hardware or I/O.

TCP_NODELAY and Nagle's Algorithm
: If you're experiencing a bottleneck of around 25 requests/sec or 40ms per call, it might be due to TCP_NODELAY or Nagle's algorithm. These can be disabled using environment variables to improve performance.
Tools & Libraries
strace
: A Linux utility for inspecting system calls made by a process (doesn't require root).
django-neopolitan
: Use the
CRUDView
for easy CRUD views (from the first htmx talk).
django-auto-prefetch
: Automatically prefetches related objects to reduce DB queries.
GitHub

: Content Security Policy for django -- is going to be merged into Django core.

: Enables Face ID or fingerprint login (passkey support).

PyPI

: Recommended for blocking "bad people" (not just bots) using their database.

在性能测试方面，强调编写性能测试以检测视图执行时间，并建议对比本地和云服务器的IO速度以找出瓶颈。还讨论了使用 `strace` 等工具进行系统调用检查，以及通过 `django-neopolitan` 和 `django-auto-prefetch` 等库减少数据库查询。

最佳实践包括在PR中审查SQL迁移文件，计算测试中的数据库查询数量，以及清理旧的功能标志。社区方面，介绍了Django Admin的高度定制案例和用Rust编写的Django模板后端。总体而言，会议展示了Django社区的创新和实用解决方案。

data.title: Why Momentum Works (2017)
data.author: vector_spaces
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了动量（Momentum）在梯度下降算法中的作用及其原理。传统观点认为动量通过减缓振荡和加速迭代来加快收敛，但作者指出，动量还有其他重要行为，如允许更大的步长范围并产生自身的振荡。文章使用凸二次模型来更精确地理解动量，指出梯度下降在面对病态曲率时会减慢进度，而动量通过引入短期记忆来加速迭代，实现“加速”效果。动量不仅能解决梯度下降的某些问题，还在某些函数上提供二次加速，具备最优性质。文章强调动量不是简单的技巧，而是具备深刻的数学美感。

主要讨论点：关于物理学中惯性与动量的本质、数值优化方法的比较，以及对文章质量和相关资源的讨论。

不同观点：
• [billfruit] 提出关于旋转运动的疑问，询问在没有摩擦和空气阻力的情况下，轮子是否会永远旋转下去。这涉及到理想状态下的物理运动问题，特别是关于能量守恒和无耗散系统的讨论。
• [Lerc] 对物理学中的惯性和动量本质提出深刻疑问，引用费曼的故事，表达了对物理现象背后深层次原因的思考。同时，也对“位置”这个概念在时空中的本质表示困惑，反映了在理解物理基本概念时的困难。
• [shoo] 则关注数值优化中的动量方法，通过实际操作和代码实验，比较了不同优化方法（如CG和BFGS）在解决特定函数最小化问题上的效率。讨论了动量方法与线搜索方法的差异，并引用了相关的文献和算法实现。

补充讨论：
• [dang] 提供了一个过去讨论的链接，指向2017年关于“为什么动量有效”的讨论，暗示该话题在之前已有深入探讨。
• [porridgeraisin] 对文章的质量表示赞赏，但同时表达了对内容创作方Distill.pub不再活跃的遗憾。
• [muro] 简单地对文章的制作质量表示肯定，赞赏作者的努力。
• [timewizard] 对文章的表达方式持批评态度，认为文章写得有些杂乱。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在对惯性和动量这些基本物理概念的深层次理解上，特别是Lerc对惯性现象背后原因的困惑，以及其他用户对数值优化方法效率的实际操作体验与理论分析的差异。

Why Momentum Really Works
Step-size α = 0.02
Momentum β = 0.99
We often think of Momentum as a means of dampening oscillations and speeding up the iterations, leading to faster convergence. But it has other interesting behavior. It allows a larger range of step-sizes to be used, and creates its own oscillations. What is going on?
Gabriel Goh
UC Davis
April. 4
2017
Citation:
Goh, 2017
Here’s a popular story about momentum
[1, 2, 3]
: gradient descent is a man walking down a hill. He follows the steepest path downwards; his progress is slow, but steady. Momentum is a heavy ball rolling down the same hill. The added inertia acts both as a smoother and an accelerator, dampening oscillations and causing us to barrel through narrow valleys, small humps and local minima.
This standard story isn’t wrong, but it fails to explain many important behaviors of momentum. In fact, momentum can be understood far more precisely if we study it on the right model.
One nice model is the convex quadratic. This model is rich enough to reproduce momentum’s local dynamics in real problems, and yet simple enough to be understood in closed form. This balance gives us powerful traction for understanding this algorithm.
We begin with gradient descent. The algorithm has many virtues, but speed is not one of them. It is simple — when optimizing a smooth function

For a step-size small enough, gradient descent makes a monotonic improvement at every iteration. It always converges, albeit to a local minimum. And under a few weak curvature conditions it can even get there at an exponential rate.
But the exponential decrease, though appealing in theory, can often be infuriatingly small. Things often begin quite well — with an impressive, almost immediate decrease in the loss. But as the iterations progress, things start to slow down. You start to get a nagging feeling you’re not making as much progress as you should be. What has gone wrong?
The problem could be the optimizer’s old nemesis, pathological curvature. Pathological curvature is, simply put, regions of
f

which aren’t scaled properly. The landscapes are often described as valleys, trenches, canals and ravines. The iterates either jump between valleys, or approach the optimum in small, timid steps. Progress along certain directions grind to a halt. In these unfortunate regions, gradient descent fumbles.
Momentum proposes the following tweak to gradient descent. We give gradient descent a short-term memory:

Optimizers call this minor miracle “acceleration”.
The new algorithm may seem at first glance like a cheap hack. A simple trick to get around gradient descent’s more aberrant behavior — a smoother for oscillations between steep canyons. But the truth, if anything, is the other way round. It is gradient descent which is the hack. First, momentum gives up to a quadratic speedup on many functions.

This is no small matter — this is similar to the speedup you get from the Fast Fourier Transform, Quicksort, and Grover’s Algorithm. When the universe gives you quadratic speedups, you should start to pay attention.
But there’s more. A lower bound, courtesy of Nesterov
[5]

data.title: Running Clojure in WASM with GraalVM
data.author: roman01la
data.article_summary: GraalVM v25开始支持WASM后端，使得Java和Clojure程序可以编译为WASM。尽管WASM后端尚不支持多线程和网络功能，但已能编译和运行单线程计算程序。例如，简单的Clojure "Hello, World!" 程序可以在浏览器中运行。其WASM二进制文件大小为5.6MB，压缩后约2.5MB。使用`wasm-opt`工具优化后可减少约600KB。分析显示，70%的二进制内容是堆快照，多数方法来自Java命名空间。WASM版本的性能比原生编译版本慢2-3倍，比ClojureScript版本慢5倍。GraalVM还支持WASM与JavaScript的互操作。
data.comments_summary:

• **GraalVM未被足够重视**：tiffanyh指出GraalVM技术上非常出色，但未得到足够关注，特别是GraalVM从v25开始支持WASM，这表明了对GraalVM在WASM领域应用的认可和期待。

43810211.article_content:
Starting from v25
GraalVM
added support for
WASM
backend for Java programs compiled to native image, which means that it's finally becomes possible to compile and run
Clojure
programs in WASM!
Although WASM backend is in its early days, and
doesn't support threading and networking
, it is already possible to compile and run single-threaded computational programs in Java/Clojure.
If you open browser console now, on this page, you'll see
Hello, World!
printed in the console. That's a Clojure program talking to you :)
(ns core
(:gen-class))
(defn -main [& args]
(println "Hello, World!"))
Binary size
The output WASM of this simple program is 5.6MB binary, which can be pruned a bit via
wasm-opt
tool
, just make sure that it doesn't break anything for you. Luckily when compressed (gzip, brotli, etc) the binary becomes just ~2.5MB in size.
After running the binary through wasm-opt I got 5MB output, so roughly ~600KB less ones and zeroes.
wasm-opt core.js.wasm -o core.js.wasm -Oz --enable-gc --enable-strings --enable-reference-types --enable-exception-handling --enable-bulk-memory --enable-nontrapping-float-to-int
In comparison, this basic hello world program in Java results in just 1MB of WASM.
public class Main {
public static void main(String[] args) {
System.out.println("Hello, World!");
}
}
To give you a sense of how binary size changes with added libraries, using
clojure.data.json
increases WASM binary by 130KB. Note that if a namespace is required but never used, it's pruned from the output.
(ns core
(:require [clojure.data.json :as json])
(:gen-class))
(defn -main [& args]
(prn (json/write-str {:a 1 :b 2})))
For detailed analysis GraalVM provides a build report, that says that 70% of compiled output is heap snapshot and roughly 50% of it is filled with strings and hash maps.
It's interesting that number of methods chanrt shows that majority, 60% of methods are coming from various Java namespaces, while Clojure only occupies 17% of methods.
Here's the full interactive build report of the WASM binary running on this page.
Speed
Running unoptimized binary via Node 23.9.0
- big reduce:         {:total-ops 10**1, :total-time 2.6s, :per-op-time 256.3ms}
- int/float division: {:total-ops 10**7, :total-time 763.2ms, :per-op-time 76ns}
- float division:     {:total-ops 10**7, :total-time 398.9ms, :per-op-time 39ns}
- integer division:   {:total-ops 10**7, :total-time 45.2ms, :per-op-time 4ns}
Optimized binary runs about 10% faster.
wasm-opt core.js.wasm -o core.js.wasm -O4 --enable-gc --enable-strings --enable-reference-types --enable-exception-handling --enable-bulk-memory --enable-nontrapping-float-to-int
- big reduce:         {:total-ops 10**1, :total-time 2.3s, :per-op-time 226.0ms}
- int/float division: {:total-ops 10**7, :total-time 646.6ms, :per-op-time 64ns}
- float division:     {:total-ops 10**7, :total-time 348.0ms, :per-op-time 34ns}
- integer division:   {:total-ops 10**7, :total-time 45.3ms, :per-op-time 4ns}
You can run the benchmark yourself on this page, press the button below and wait for logs in the console

43810211.article_summary: GraalVM v25开始支持WASM后端，使得Java和Clojure程序可以编译为WASM。尽管WASM后端尚不支持多线程和网络功能，但已能编译和运行单线程计算程序。例如，简单的Clojure "Hello, World!" 程序可以在浏览器中运行。其WASM二进制文件大小为5.6MB，压缩后约2.5MB。使用`wasm-opt`工具优化后可减少约600KB。分析显示，70%的二进制内容是堆快照，多数方法来自Java命名空间。WASM版本的性能比原生编译版本慢2-3倍，比ClojureScript版本慢5倍。GraalVM还支持WASM与JavaScript的互操作。

不同观点：
• **支持CheerpJ**：apignotti提到CheerpJ可以运行JVM语言（包括Clojure）在浏览器中，支持多线程、反射和Swing/AWT应用，甚至可以运行Minecraft。这表明CheerpJ在跨平台Java应用上的强大功能和实际应用案例。

• **支持GraalVM**：nzoschke分享了使用GraalVM将Java项目与Go结合的实践，特别是通过GraalVM生成原生二进制文件，并希望未来WASM支持UDP网络和多线程，以便转向WASM。这显示了GraalVM在跨语言开发和逆向工程中的应用潜力，以及对WASM未来发展的期待。

• **GraalVM未被足够重视**：tiffanyh指出GraalVM技术上非常出色，但未得到足够关注，特别是GraalVM从v25开始支持WASM，这表明了对GraalVM在WASM领域应用的认可和期待。

data.title: OpenAI Adds Shopping to ChatGPT in a Challenge to Google
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary: OpenAI宣布将通过ChatGPT推出购物功能，用户可直接在AI搜索查询中看到购物按钮，无需登录账户。用户无法在ChatGPT内完成购买，需跳转至商家网站进行交易。产品推荐基于用户的偏好及网络评价，目前推荐结果为有机结果，非付费广告。购物体验更加个性化和对话式，不同于谷歌购物的关键词匹配。推荐产品时，ChatGPT会参考包括WIRED等出版物的评测以及Reddit等用户论坛的内容。关于 affiliate 收入，OpenAI表示将尝试多种模式，但目前首要任务是提升用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）结果是否会像搜索引擎和社交媒体一样被商业化，是否会出现付费推广和广告影响结果的客观性。

不同观点：
• **对LLM商业化的担忧**：
  - [Tangokat] 和 [mk89] 提到，LLM模型可能会像搜索引擎一样，结果逐渐被优化用于销售产品和增加参与度，甚至可能变得难以区分是否包含广告。
  - [xdfgh1112] 强调，现有的搜索引擎已经被过度商业化，搜索普通词汇都会被解读为产品相关，担心ChatGPT也会如此。

• **LLM的实用价值与商业化之间的平衡**：
  - [sethhochberg] 认为LLM在初期非常有用，但随着商业利益介入，可能会逐渐变得不那么实用。他举例说明了在使用ChatGPT进行家装设计时的便利性，但也提到了如果工具能直接帮助购买产品会更高效。
  
• **对结果客观性的质疑**：
  - [caseyy] 和 [bluedevilzn] 以讽刺的语气表达了对结果中立性的怀疑，认为最终可能会偏向于付费推广的产品。
  
• **对技术实现的疑问**：
  - [Imnimo] 对ChatGPT的搜索机制提出疑问，不清楚它是否使用带有广告的搜索引擎（如Bing），并关心广告内容是否被移除。

• **对技术进步的调侃**：
  - [SirMaster] 以幽默方式表达了对技术进步的期待，但也暗示了市场现实（如高价显卡）可能会影响技术的实际体验。

补充讨论：
- **学术研究支持**：[Tangokat] 引用了学术论文，指出已经有研究表明LLM可以为参与度进行优化，暗示未来可能会更倾向于商业化用途。
- **对免费版本的担忧**：[xdfgh122] 提到免费版本可能会更倾向于商业化，暗示用户体验可能会因此下降。

争议焦点：LLM模型是否会像搜索引擎一样被广告和商业化影响，进而失去其中立性和实用性。

43824952.article_content:
Save this story
Save
Save this story
Save
OpenAI announced today that users will soon be able to buy products through
ChatGPT
. The rollout of shopping buttons for
AI-powered search
queries will come to everyone, whether they are a signed-in user or not. Shoppers will not be able to check out inside of ChatGPT; instead they will be redirected to the merchant’s website to finish the transaction.
In a prelaunch demo for WIRED, Adam Fry, the ChatGPT search product lead at
OpenAI
, demonstrated how the updated user experience could be used to help people using the tool for product research decide which
espresso machine
or
office chair
to buy. The product recommendations shown to prospective shoppers are based on what ChatGPT remembers about a user’s preferences as well as product reviews pulled from across the web.
Fry says ChatGPT users are already running over a billion
web searches
per week, and that people are using the tool to research a wide breadth of shopping categories, like beauty, home goods, and electronics. The product results in ChatGPT for
best office chairs
, one of WIRED’s rigorously tested and widely read buying guides, included a link to our reporting in the sources tab. (Although the business side of Condé Nast, WIRED’s parent company, signed a
licensing deal
last year with OpenAI so the company can surface our content, the editorial team retains independence in how we cover the startup.)
Searching for espresso machines inside ChatGPT.
Image Courtesy of OpenAI
The new user experience of buying stuff inside of ChatGPT shares many similarities to
Google Shopping
. In the interfaces of both, when you click on the image of a budget office chair that tickles your fancy, multiple retailers, like Amazon and Walmart, are listed on the right side of the screen, with buttons for completing the purchase. There is one major difference between shopping through ChatGPT versus Google, for now: The results you see in OpenAI searches are not paid placements, but organic results. “They are not ads,” says Fry. “They are not sponsored.”
While some product recommendations that appear inside of Google Shopping show up because retailers paid for them to be there, that’s just one mechanism Google uses to decide which products to list in Shopping searches. Websites that publish product reviews are constantly tweaking the content of their buying recommendations in an effort to convince the opaque Google algorithm that the website includes high-quality reviews of products that have been thoroughly tested by real humans. Google favors those more considered reviews in search results and will rank them highly when a user is researching a product. To land one of the top spots in a Google search can lead to more of those users buying the product through the website, potentially earning the publisher millions of dollars in affiliate revenue.
So how does ChatGPT choose which products to recommend? Why were those specific espresso machines and office chairs listed first when the user typed the prompt?
“It’s not looking for specific signals that are in some algorithm,” says Fry. According to him, this will be a shopping experience that’s more personalized and conversational, rather than keyword-focused. “It's trying to understand how people are reviewing this, how people are talking about this, what the pros and cons are,” says Fry. If you say that you prefer only buying black clothes from a specific retailer, then ChatGPT will supposedly store that information in
its memory
the next time you ask for advice about what shirt to buy, giving you recommendations that align with your tastes.
The reviews that ChatGPT features for products will pull from a blend of online sources, including editorial publishers like WIRED as well as user-generated forums like Reddit. Fry says that users can tell ChatGPT which types of reviews to prioritize when curating a list of recommended products.
One of the most pressing questions for online publishers with this new release is likely how affiliate revenue will work in this situation. Currently, if you read WIRED’s review of the best office chairs and decide to purchase one through our link, we get a cut of the revenue and it supports our journalism. How will
affiliate revenue
work inside of ChatGPT shopping when the tool recommends an office chair that OpenAI knows is a good pick because WIRED, among others, gave it a good review?
“We are going to be experimenting with a whole bunch of different ways that this can work,” says Fry. He didn’t share specific plans, saying that providing high-quality recommendations is OpenAI’s first priority right now, and that the company might try different affiliate revenue models in the future.
When asked if he sees this as potentially a meaningful revenue driver in the long term, Fry similarly says that OpenAI is just focused on the user experience first and will iterate on ChatGPT shopping as the startup learns more post-release. OpenAI has big revenue goals;

data.title: The One-Person Framework in Practice
data.author: frans
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同开发框架的比较与选择，以及在个人或小型开发环境中的适用性

不同观点：
• **jhancock**：认为Rails和Phoenix适合传统Web 2.0应用开发，但在特定问题空间（如Clojure）中，这些框架可能不是最佳选择。强调了框架选择应根据具体需求，而不应局限于流行框架。
• **kukkeliskuu**：分享了使用Django构建大型ERP系统的经验，强调了简单性和避免不必要复杂性的重要性，使用传统的HTML和少量JavaScript（如AlpineJS/HTMX）来提升效率。
• **hi_hi**：选择了AdonisJS（类似Rails的Node.js框架），因为其类似Rails的体验和Node生态系统的优势，特别是类型安全性。
• **alankarmisra**：认为开发人员的个人能力比框架更重要，框架只是工具，个人经验和开发风格对生产力影响更大。
• **searls**：通过Rails 7+的案例研究，强调Rails对个人开发者的帮助，尤其是在开发大型应用时。
• **xutopia**：使用Rails和Hotwire Native构建移动应用，强调了Rails生态系统的全面性和适应性。
• **hdjrudni**：认为框架选择并不至关重要，市场上流行的框架都有足够的支持，真正的挑战在于业务层面。
• **sillycube**：认为市场需求比框架选择更重要，框架本身无法挽救失败的项目。
• **connectsnk**：寻求Ruby on Rails之外的快速开发框架，强调了配置约定对开发速度的影响。
• **sebstefan**：希望得到其他技术（如PHP）开发者的意见，比较Rails是否显著优越。
• **ndneighbor**：认为Ruby语言的易学易用性是Rails受欢迎的原因之一，但Elixir/Phoenix也受到不少关注。
• **Glyptodon**：强调了在前端技术选择上的决策对整体生产力的影响，认为避免复杂的React前端可以显著提升效率。
• **rambambram**：支持使用结构良好的单体应用，认为个人的决策能力对项目成功至关重要。
• **jokethrowaway**：认为个人能力和多角色适应性比框架选择更重要，技术堆栈的自动化可以减少时间消耗。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于框架对生产力的影响程度，部分开发者认为个人能力比框架选择更重要，而另一些开发者则强调了特定框架（如Rails）在快速开发中的优势。
• 不同框架（如Rails、Django、AdonisJS、Phoenix）在不同场景下的适用性被广泛讨论，尤其是对于个人开发者和小型团队。
• 简单性和避免不必要的复杂性被认为是选择框架和前端技术的重要考量因素。
• 市场需求和项目成功的关联被提及，强调了技术选择之外的商业因素对项目成败的影响。

通过这些观点，可以看出开发框架的选择是一个多维度的问题，涉及技术特性、个人能力和市场需求等多方面因素。

data.title: One Million Chessboards
data.author: chunkles
data.article_summary: 《One Million Chessboards》是一个由个人开发者创建的网站，包含一百万个国际象棋棋盘，所有用户可以实时、无回合地移动任何棋盘上的棋子。该项目受其之前作品《One Million Checkboxes》启发，但在技术上更具挑战性。整个游戏运行在单个服务器上，棋盘状态存储在内存中，采用2D数组形式，后端使用Go语言编写。游戏通过 websockets 传输状态快照和更新，并采用乐观处理和回滚机制来处理冲突移动。客户端按区域分组接收更新，以减少服务器负担。项目发布后8小时内，用户已进行了约130万次移动，服务器负载极低。用户可以随时访问网站参与游戏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大规模多人在线国际象棋游戏的玩法、技术实现及规则争议

不同观点：
• NelsonMinar认为游戏展现了涌现式玩法（emergent gameplay），即游戏规则简单但通过大规模互动产生了有趣的可能性。他赞赏eieio的项目设计，尤其是其不可预见的玩法。
• eieio（项目创建者）回应称项目旨在处理大规模并发操作，使用Golang语言实现了每秒处理上万次移动，并愿意解答技术细节问题。
• sltkr遇到了技术问题，游戏崩溃并报错，具体指出了代码中的错误位置。
• nomilk分享了一次有趣的游戏经历，提到有人用大量棋子保护国王并成功反击，展示了游戏中策略的多样性。
• yayitswei预测游戏将演变为机器人（bot）战争，并分享了一段用于推进士兵的代码，暗示了游戏自动化潜力。
• mdaniel对跨棋盘的移动和捕获规则感到困惑，认为虽然规模宏大，但游戏规则有些不一致。
• pavel_lishin期望每个棋盘有单独的回合，并对能够随意选择棋盘和棋子感到意外，认为这种设计不够传统。
• ryukoposting享受追逐玩家的乐趣，认为这种玩法即便不遵循传统象棋规则也很有趣。
• GenshoTikamura对游戏的最终结局感到好奇，猜测可能会是僵局或激烈的对决，反映了游戏结果的不确定性。
• sashank_1509提到花了半小时构建了一个坚不可摧的黑棋阵型，希望它能坚持到最后，显示了玩家对策略的投入。
• pmontra表示游戏在其安卓设备上运行良好，赞扬了游戏的兼容性。
• darepublic遇到了规则理解问题，不确定规则是否被严格执行，质疑游戏是否只是更新而非实时对抗。
• maxmcd提到了与该项目相关的另一个项目“One Million Checkboxes”的故事，并请求eieio开源Go代码以供研究。

补充讨论：
- 游戏的技术实现，尤其是Golang在处理大规模并发上的优势（eieio的解释）。
- 游戏规则的模糊和不确定性，尤其是跨棋盘的移动和捕获机制引发的争议（mdaniel和pavel_lishin的观点）。
- 玩家对游戏策略的深度投入和享受，尤其是涌现式玩法带来的不可预见性（NelsonMinar和sashank_1509的反馈）。
- 对游戏自动化和机器人战争的潜在发展方向的预测（yayitswei的观点）。

43825336.article_content:
One Million Chessboards
a million chessboards that anyone can play on
Apr 28, 2025
I made a website. It’s called
One Million Chessboards
. It has one million chessboards on it.
Moving a piece moves it for everyone, instantly. There are no turns. You can move between boards.
Loading...
moving some pieces
What
Well last year I made this game called
One Million Checkboxes
.
It was a pretty fun time! So I thought I’d do something like this again.
I worked really hard on this one. I hope you like it.
How
This was the most technically challenging thing that I’ve worked on in a long time. I’m going to save a full technical writeup until I see how my decisions pan out, since I think there’s a decent chance I’ll need to make a lot of changes.
But I’ll summarize a few things for you.
Unlike One Million Checkboxes, I designed this for scale
The game runs on a single server (!)
The board is stored fully in-memory; it’s a 2D array of 64 million uint64s
The backend is written in go. This is my first go project.
I use a single writer thread, tons of reader threads, and coordinate access to the board with a mutex
The frontend optimistically applies all moves you make immediately. It then builds up a dependency graph of the moves you’ve made, and backs them out if it receives a conflicting update before the server acks your move.
The server ships zstd-compressed protobufs to the clients over websockets for state snapshots (approximately a 100x100 square around the client), move and capture updates, and acks/rejections for moves
Clients are grouped into 50x50 “zones” and only receive moves for zones adjacent to their current zone
Clients fetch global data (game stats, the minimap, etc) by polling via GET; data is cached in Cloudflare with a low TTL so this is much cheaper than shipping it over every websocket
That last part - optimistic move application with what games people sometimes call “rollback” - is about 1,600 lines of code that took me a ~7 days of fulltime work to write. I don’t remember the last time I wrestled with a problem that hard!
As of 8 PM, 8 hours after launch, players have made about 1.3 million moves and there are about 400 concurrent users most of the time. Load on my server is neglibible!
Can I play
Yes!
Play it here
.
I really hope you like this one. More updates to come :)

data.title: The 12-bit rainbow palette
data.author: rguiscard
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了12位彩虹调色板的设计过程，专为National Grid: Live设计，包含12种颜色，考虑了人眼对亮度、色度和色相的感知。调色板使用12位色彩深度，每个颜色用四个字符的十六进制代码表示，如#817。与RGB色彩空间不同，LCH色彩空间根据亮度、色度和色相定义颜色，更符合人眼感知。简单RGB彩虹调色板在相邻颜色间亮度变化大，而LCH调色板通过控制亮度变化，使黄色最亮，红色和蓝色适中，避免了不良视觉效果。尽管12位色彩深度限制了可用颜色，但通过微调亮度、色度和色相，最终调色板实现了色相均匀分布、色度变化小、亮度平滑过渡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：选择视觉上可区分的颜色，特别是在需要大量颜色时遇到的挑战及解决方案

不同观点：
• Sammi认为选择少量颜色不难，但当需要20到30种颜色时就变得困难，并分享了一个可能的解决方案链接。
• jasonthorsness赞赏了该调色板，并介绍了使用CSS中新增的颜色功能（如oklch）来表示这些颜色，强调了这些新功能在创建调色板时的优势。
• zeroq指出Cynthia Brewer在信息图颜色方案上的研究，并批评了一些设计师使用“神圣几何”和RGB颜色空间来解释颜色关系的方法。他还提到了Kubelka和Munk的颜色混合算法。
• barrkel和otikik提到调色板中某些颜色对色盲不友好，特别是两种绿色和几种蓝色及洋红色在区分上有困难。
• whall6质疑调色板两端颜色过于相似，认为在渐变中最大和最小颜色应更易区分。
• NelsonMinar讨论了12位颜色限制的挑战，指出ColorBrewer只到9种颜色，并提到色盲问题。
• BugsJustFindMe认为调色板中颜色的差异不均匀，需要更多考虑。
• hedora从技术角度讨论了该调色板相当于3.5849625位，并解释了添加其他元素后的位数。
• jjmarr对12位颜色用4个字符表示提出疑问，认为应该用3个十六进制数字表示。
• cdev_gl赞赏项目并希望了解使用12位编码的原因，对有限位深颜色空间的表现感兴趣。
• kazinator对LCH颜色空间进行了进一步的学术探讨，引用了维基百科上的相关资料。

补充讨论：
• jjgreen提供了其他格式和资源的链接（cpt-city），扩展了调色板的获取途径。
• zeroq对颜色理论和设计师常用方法的批评引发对更科学颜色选择方法的讨论。
• 色盲问题成为争议焦点，特别是调色板在实际应用中的可访问性受到关注。

43827108.article_content:
The 12-bit rainbow palette
I designed the 12-bit rainbow palette for use on
National Grid: Live
. It consists of twelve colours chosen with consideration for how we perceive luminance, chroma, and hue:
The palette uses a 12-bit colour depth, so each colour requires only four characters when specified as a hexadecimal colour code in a
CSS
or
SVG
file:
#817
#a35
#c66
#e94
#ed0
#9d5
#4d8
#2cb
#0bc
#09c
#36b
#639
Designing the palette
Computers define colours in terms of red, green, and blue components, which are treated equally. However, we perceive these components as having differing luminance: compared to a pure red, a pure green looks much brighter and a pure blue looks much darker. As a result, a simple
RGB
rainbow palette has large changes in luminance between neighbouring colours. This can be seen by converting colours to greys of equal perceived luminance:
The
LCH
colour space is an alternative to the
RGB
colour space that defines colours in terms of luminance, chroma, and hue components. These components are perceptually uniform, which means that a change by a particular numerical amount will be perceived similarly for any colour.
An
LCH
rainbow colour palette can be created by choosing fixed chroma and luminance values and varying the hue. However, the resulting palette looks unpleasant because yellow is darkened to brown, red is lightened to pink, and blue becomes very pale.
A better approach is to allow the luminance to vary, but in a controlled way. Yellow is given the highest luminance, as it only looks yellow when bright. After choosing two other colours — a red and a blue in this case — the luminance can then be calculated for the other hues.
Using a 12-bit colour depth limits the available colours, so slight changes to luminance, chroma, and hue must be made, but these are small enough not to be noticeable. The resulting palette has evenly-spaced hues, only small variations in chroma, and smoothly increasing and decreasing luminance:

data.title: Legal art forgery, for the sake of movies (2014)
data.author: theneedful
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讲述了在电影《巴斯奎特》中复制名画《格尔尼卡》的复杂过程。由于无法直接使用原作或海报，电影制作团队必须 painstakingly 手工复制名画。 scenic artist Michael Stockton 花了三周时间复制毕加索的《格尔尼卡》，但最终却不得不将其销毁。这是因为电影中使用著名画作涉及繁琐的版权和权利审批流程，且销毁过程也受特定规则约束。

过去，艺术图像的权利管理较松，但因两起重大版权诉讼，如今变得更加严格。在《巴斯奎特》中，由于巴斯奎特的遗产方索要高额费用，电影制作团队只能模仿其风格创作假画。导演朱利安·施纳贝尔亲自参与绘画，还从自己的收藏中提供了一些作品，包括安迪·沃霍尔的真品。而《格尔尼卡》的复制则因毕加索家族的特别许可而得以实现，但最终仍需销毁以遵守协议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术作品的复制与版权问题

不同观点：
• **[analog31的观点]**：在1950年代，复制著名画作是艺术训练的一部分，博物馆甚至允许在展览厅内设立画架进行临摹。然而，现在由于安全问题或版权问题，这种做法似乎已经不再被允许。这暗示了时代变化对艺术教育和实践的影响。

• **[gitroom的观点]**：对版权相关的繁文缛节感到不满，认为这些规定限制了艺术欣赏和创作的自由。他希望能够简单地欣赏艺术和创作，而不必面对复杂的法律限制。

• **[colechristensen的观点]**：批评现行的知识产权法对艺术作品的保护时间过长，尤其是当原作者的后代已经不再直接依赖这些作品谋生时。他建议采用难以察觉的防伪水印来防止欺诈性销售，而不是全面的法律保护。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：版权法的适用范围和期限问题。colechristensen认为现行的知识产权法对艺术作品的保护时间过于长久，尤其是在原作者的后代已经不再依赖这些作品的情况下，而analog31则通过历史实例表明版权和安全问题如何影响艺术实践。

• **历史背景**：analog31提供了20世纪中叶艺术教育中复制名画的做法，为讨论提供了历史背景，显示出不同时期对艺术复制行为的接受程度不同。

• **个人体验**：analog31分享了个人经历，增强了其观点的说服力，而gitroom则表达了对版权复杂性的个人反感，这代表了一部分公众对法律限制的普遍情绪。

• **具体案例**：colechristensen引用了关于毕加索作品的电影案例，以具体实例支持其对版权法的批评，并提出了替代方案。

总体来看，讨论围绕着版权法对艺术创作和欣赏的影响，以及是否需要进行法律改革以平衡保护和创作自由。

Imagine this: You’ve just spent three weeks painstakingly replicating a Picasso painting from scratch—you’ve scrutinized documentation about the artist’s creative process; you’ve practiced his brushstrokes, so your work will look convincing; you’ve even painted in noted preliminary images, then covered them up, because that’s what he did. You’ve toiled over this, all for mere seconds of screen time in a film.
And then you have to destroy it.
Such was the case for scenic artist Michael Stockton’s copy of
Guernica
, in the film
Basquiat
. Turns out, when you want to feature a famous painting in a movie, you can't simply slap a poster of a Monet or a Picasso in a frame and yell, “Action!”—nor can you cart the real thing from its space on a museum wall to the set (there’s too much margin for loss or destruction). The task is often a “thorny challenge,” as described by
Basquiat

这篇文章讲述了在电影《巴斯奎特》中复制名画《格尔尼卡》的复杂过程。由于无法直接使用原作或海报，电影制作团队必须 painstakingly 手工复制名画。 scenic artist Michael Stockton 花了三周时间复制毕加索的《格尔尼卡》，但最终却不得不将其销毁。这是因为电影中使用著名画作涉及繁琐的版权和权利审批流程，且销毁过程也受特定规则约束。

data.title: Packed Data Support in Haskell
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Haskell中对"压缩数据"（packed data）格式的支持。传统上，数据在网络传输或持久化时需要序列化（如JSON或XML），接收时需要反序列化，这既耗时又增加数据体积。文章提出一种二进制压缩数据格式，可以在发送和接收数据时跳过这些步骤，直接使用数据，提高效率，尤其是减少指针跳转，更好地利用L1缓存。

文章介绍了一个名为`packed-data`的Haskell库，它利用类型系统和模板Haskell实现数据的打包、解包和遍历，而无需修改编译器。该库自动生成代码，支持任意数据类型的打包与解包，并提供自定义的模式匹配功能。关键概念包括`NeedsBuilder`类型，它通过phantom types控制打包过程中的数据需求。

这一方法受到Cap'n Proto等项目的启发，但Haskell是首个通过纯类型系统实现该功能的语言。

Contents
Packed Data support in Haskell
This blog post aims to be a short and accessible summary of a paper that will be published at ECOOP 2025, titled
Type-safe and portable support for packed data
.
Introduction: Packed Data
When programs want to persist data or send it over the network, they need to
serialise
it (e.g. to JSON or XML). On the other hand, when a program receives data from the network or reads it from a file, data needs to be
deserialised
.
flowchart LR
Server(["Server"])
Server --> SD["Serialise"]
SD -- Network --- RD["Deserialise"]
RD --> Client(["Client"])
These de/serialisation steps are necessary because
we cannot use the in-memory representation/layout of the data in a file or when sending it over the network
, mainly because of the pointers it may contain.
Consequently,
de/serialising data has a cost
: it takes time, and the serialised version of the data is usually bigger than its in-memory representation. In the context of systems that interact through the network, it leads to
larger payloads
to send, and thus
slower transfer times
.
Now,
what if we didn’t have to serialise the data before sending it to a client
, and
what if the client could use the data from the network as-is
, without any marshalling steps? We could save some time, on both the server and client side.
Introducing the
‘packed’ data format
, a binary format that allows using data as it is, without the need for a deserialisation step. A notable perk of this format is that
traversals on packed trees is proven to be faster than on ‘unpacked’ trees
: as the fields of data structures are inlines, there are no pointer jumps, thus making the most of the L1 cache.
To better understand how it looks like, here is a representation of a tree in memory that uses pointers.
N
represents nodes, and
L
represents leaves. Numbers are the tree’s data, and dots and arrows are pointers.
Pointer-based tree layout in memory
Here is what a packed tree looks like in memory.
Packed tree layout in memory
A few projects use or leverage this ‘packed’ approach. For example, Cap’n Proto
1
is a popular library that allows packing data (i.e. build a binary buffer containing the data), using that buffer as-is (e.g. traverse it and ‘unpack’ fields of a structure). However, no languages support packed data natively. Haskell does support compact normal forms (CNF), but the
Compact
data type does not allow using (e.g. deconstructing) packed values. We should note the existence of
Gibbon
, a research compiler that accepts functional programs and generates programs that use packed data natively.
Unfortunately
the use of packed data is limited to research projects
, probably because it’s kinda hard to support it.
In this post, I will introduce
the
packed-data
Haskell library
. It
allows packing and unpacking data, as well as traversing packed data as-is
(with a custom
case
function), with no marshalling step or compiler mods, thanks to the power of types. As far as we are aware, this is on of the first effort to bring support for packed data using only the host language’s type-system, meta-programming (Template Haskell)
with no compiler modifications
.

the data, thanks to a generated

data.title: Requirements change until they don't
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在系统需求不断变化的情况下，形式化方法（Formal Methods）的应用及其挑战。作者指出，尽管需求经常变化，初期的高正确性要求（通过形式化方法实现）可能显得不切实际或成本过高，但最终系统需要满足稳定性和长期支持的要求。文章借用物理学中的“相变”概念，说明软件架构在面对负载或复杂性增加时需要转型，而这种转型可能引入新的错误。形式化方法可用于确保系统在变化过程中保持关键属性，如一致性和线性化。作者强调，在进行系统变更时，确保不破坏现有客户需求是至关重要的，这也是形式化方法的一个重要应用场景。简言之，软件维护复杂，形式化方法有助于管理系统演进中的关键属性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的方法论和实践，包括敏捷开发、形式化验证（Formal Verification, FV）以及开发过程中的不同阶段和需求变化。

不同观点：
• **taeric** 认为，软件开发中的不同阶段（如学习、构建）类似于物质的相变，不同阶段有不同的特性和挑战。他建议使用建筑隐喻（如脚手架和关键石）来理解学习过程，并指出软件开发中试图将解决方案和构建模型完全融合会导致复杂性。他质疑如何将这些概念应用于形式化方法，通常通过不同层次的形式化以及确认合规性的流程来实现。

• **firesteelrain** 针对敏捷开发中的需求变化提出观点，认为Wayne对敏捷开发的理解有误，将“需求总是变化”这一原则过于字面化。firesteelrain指出，敏捷开发是一种应对不确定性的哲学姿态，而不是预测所有需求都会无休止地变化。他强调在实际生产环境中，需求确实会因为安全、合规、用户行为和扩展等因素不断变化。

• **AndrewKemendo** 讨论了形式化验证在软件工程中的应用，认为对于业务环境中的大多数软件项目，新功能通常比形式化验证更具商业价值。除非业务需求明确要求形式化验证，否则形式化验证并不必要。他质疑形式化验证在商业软件中的实际应用，并指出自己很少见到商业软件项目采用形式化验证，除非是强制性要求或研究项目。

• **争议焦点**：形式化验证的必要性和实际应用场景。AndrewKemendo认为除非业务需求明确要求，否则形式化验证在商业软件中并不常见，而taeric则讨论了如何将不同开发阶段的特性与形式化方法结合。

• **敏捷开发的理解差异**：firesteelrain指出Wayne对敏捷开发中需求变化的理解有误，强调敏捷是一种应对不确定性的方法，而不是对需求无休止变化的预测。

43825958.article_content:
April 24, 2025
Requirements change until they don't
Requirements, phase changes, and formal methods.
Recently I got a question on formal methods
1
: how does it help to mathematically model systems when the system requirements are constantly changing? It doesn't make sense to spend a lot of time proving a design works, and then deliver the product and find out it's not at all what the client needs. As the saying goes, the hard part is "building the right thing", not "building the thing right".
One possible response: "why write tests"? You shouldn't write tests,
especially
lots of unit tests ahead of time
, if you might just throw them all away when the requirements change.
This is a bad response because we all know the difference between writing tests and formal methods: testing is
easy
and FM is
hard
. Testing requires low cost for moderate correctness, FM requires high(ish) cost for high correctness. And when requirements are constantly changing, "high(ish) cost" isn't affordable and "high correctness" isn't worthwhile, because a kinda-okay solution that solves a customer's problem is infinitely better than a solid solution that doesn't.
But eventually you get something that solves the problem, and what then?
Most of us don't work for Google, we can't axe features and products
on a whim
. If the client is happy with your solution, you are expected to support it. It should work when your customers run into new edge cases, or migrate all their computers to the next OS version, or expand into a market with shoddy internet. It should work when 10x as many customers are using 10x as many features. It should work when
you add new features that come into conflict
.
And just as importantly,
it should never stop solving their problem
. Canonical example: your feature involves processing requested tasks synchronously. At scale, this doesn't work, so to improve latency you make it asynchronous. Now it's eventually consistent, but your customers were depending on it being always consistent. Now it no longer does what they need, and has stopped solving their problems.
Every successful requirement met spawns a new requirement: "keep this working". That requirement is permanent, or close enough to decide our long-term strategy. It takes active investment to keep a feature behaving the same as the world around it changes.
(Is this all a pretentious of way of saying "software maintenance is hard?" Maybe!)
Phase changes
In physics there's a concept of a
phase transition
. To raise the temperature of a gram of liquid water by 1° C, you have to add 4.184 joules of energy.
2
This continues until you raise it to 100°C, then it stops. After you've added two
thousand
joules to that gram, it suddenly turns into steam. The energy of the system changes continuously but the form, or phase, changes discretely.
Software isn't physics but the idea works as a metaphor. A certain architecture handles a certain level of load, and past that you need a new architecture. Or a bunch of similar features are independently hardcoded until the system becomes too messy to understand, you remodel the internals into something unified and extendable. etc etc etc. It's doesn't have to be totally discrete phase transition, but there's definitely a "before" and "after" in the system form.
Phase changes tend to lead to more intricacy/complexity in the system, meaning it's likely that a phase change will introduce new bugs into existing behaviors. Take the synchronous vs asynchronous case. A very simple toy model of synchronous updates would be
Set(key, val)
, which updates
data[key]
to
val
.
3
A model of asynchronous updates would be
AsyncSet(key, val, priority)
adds a
(key, val, priority, server_time())
tuple to a
tasks
set, and then another process asynchronously pulls a tuple (ordered by highest priority, then earliest time) and calls
Set(key, val)
. Here are some properties the client may need preserved as a requirement:
If
AsyncSet(key, val, _, _)
is called, then
eventually
db[key] = val
(possibly violated if higher-priority tasks keep coming in)
If someone calls
AsyncSet(key1, val1, low)
and then
AsyncSet(key2, val2, low)
, they should see the first update and then the second (linearizability, possibly violated if the requests go to different servers with different clock times)
If someone calls
AsyncSet(key, val, _)
and
immediately
reads
db[key]
they should get
val
(obviously violated, though the client may accept a
slightly
weaker property)
If the new system doesn't satisfy an existing customer requirement, it's prudent to fix the bug
before
releasing the new system. The customer doesn't notice or care that your system underwent a phase change. They'll just see that one day your product solves their problems, and the next day it suddenly doesn't.
This is one of the most common applications of formal methods. Both of those systems, and every one of those properties, is formally specifiable in a specification language. We can then automatically chec
43825958.article_summary: 本文讨论了在系统需求不断变化的情况下，形式化方法（Formal Methods）的应用及其挑战。作者指出，尽管需求经常变化，初期的高正确性要求（通过形式化方法实现）可能显得不切实际或成本过高，但最终系统需要满足稳定性和长期支持的要求。文章借用物理学中的“相变”概念，说明软件架构在面对负载或复杂性增加时需要转型，而这种转型可能引入新的错误。形式化方法可用于确保系统在变化过程中保持关键属性，如一致性和线性化。作者强调，在进行系统变更时，确保不破坏现有客户需求是至关重要的，这也是形式化方法的一个重要应用场景。简言之，软件维护复杂，形式化方法有助于管理系统演进中的关键属性。

data.title: Building Small Go Containers?
data.author: randomizedcoder
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一个简单的Go程序项目（go_nix_simple），旨在测试和展示不同的容器构建方法及其性能，特别是探索Nix是否能加快构建速度。结果表明，Nix虽然能保证构建的可重复性，但并不快速。项目中加入了一些额外库（如数据库和监控工具）进行测试，发现Nix的gomod2nix并未显著提升性能。

文章还比较了使用Distroless和Scratch作为基础镜像时的构建时间、镜像大小和层数。结果显示，Scratch镜像更小，表现更优。同时，文章提到在AMD64机器上使用UPX压缩未出现问题，但有人建议可能在Apple设备上会导致构建失败。

最后，文章提供了详细的构建总结和Makefile使用指南，以帮助快速上手项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go 语言项目中使用容器和打包工具的复杂性及选择

不同观点：
• damezumari 认为整个操作令人困惑，他的 Go 容器只包含一个二进制文件，并且该文件是通过 ko 在外部构建的。他认为使用包管理器显得过于复杂，没有必要。
• tuananh 猜测可能是使用了 "scratch" 基础镜像和 "upx" 工具来实现简化的容器构建，而不是依赖复杂的包管理器。

补充讨论：
• damezumari 强调当前的做法是将所有内容打包成一个二进制文件，并直接放入容器中，避免了复杂的包管理需求。
• tuananh 则提出了一种可能的技术选择，即使用 "scratch" 这种极简的 Docker 基础镜像和 "upx" 这种可执行文件压缩工具，来进一步简化容器的大小和复杂性。
• 争议的焦点在于是否需要引入更复杂的包管理工具，还是通过现有的技术手段（如 scratch 和 upx）来达到简化构建和部署的目的。

总结来看，讨论的核心在于如何在构建 Go 项目容器时简化流程，避免不必要的复杂性。一方认为现有的二进制文件构建已经足够简单，另一方提出了可能的替代方案以进一步优化。

go_nix_simple
This is an example repo with a relatively simple
go program
.
The intention of the repo is to test/demontrate different methods for builing containers and to measure the performance.
In particular, I was interested to explore if Nix could help speedup builds.  Spoilier alert: Nix may be repeatable, but it is not fast.
The example program is essentially a
loop
printing out a counter and has prometheus counters.
I ended up adding in a bunch of other libraries (database/sql, clickhouse-go, pyroscope-go, go-redis/v9), to try to see if the nix gomod2nix improves performance.  Spoilier alert: Doesn't seem to.
The other thing this repo does is demonstrate how small the container can be.  Scratch clearly wins here, and I wonder why distroless is often recommended.
Friends on the Gopher slack suggested the upx might break the build, but I don't see evidence of this on my amd64 machine.  Maybe it breaks on Apple? Easy fix is to not use Apples.

data.title: I use zip bombs to protect my server
data.author: foxfired
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了网络中大部分流量来自机器人，其中一些是恶意机器人，如垃圾邮件发送者、内容抓取工具或黑客。作者讲述了一次其服务器因恶意机器人而成为僵尸网络的经历，并探讨了如何使用压缩炸弹（zip bomb）来防御这些机器人。压缩炸弹是一个小型的压缩文件，解压后会变得非常大，足以使机器崩溃。作者通过检测恶意请求，向这些机器人返回一个大压缩文件，使其在解压时崩溃。具体方法是使用`dd`和`gzip`命令创建压缩炸弹，并通过服务器中间件实现。虽然这种方法不能对付所有机器人，但对简单恶意的爬虫有效。使用该方法需谨慎，以免对自己设备造成损害。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应对恶意爬虫和不良网络行为的技术手段与潜在问题

不同观点：
• **恶意脚本与漏洞利用**：bilekas提到了一次由于WordPress漏洞导致恶意脚本被插入服务器的事件，这引发了对设置WordPress后快速出现安全问题的讨论。
• **崩溃攻击与防御**：ChuckMcM分享了通过让恶意SSH客户端崩溃来应对密码猜测的经历，并提到使用防火墙规则阻止不良行为者。他还介绍了使用zip炸弹来对付爬虫和AI scrapers的方法。

• **防御手段的成本与收益**：使用诸如zip炸弹等技术是否值得，特别是在可能对服务器造成更大负担的情况下，存在不同看法。

43826798.article_content:
The majority of the traffic on the web is from bots. For the most part, these bots are used to discover new content. These are RSS Feed readers, search engines crawling your content, or nowadays AI bots crawling content to power LLMs. But then there are the malicious bots. These are from spammers, content scrapers or hackers. At my old employer, a bot discovered a wordpress vulnerability and inserted a malicious script into our server. It then turned the machine into a botnet used for DDOS. One of my first websites was yanked off of Google search entirely due to bots generating spam. At some point, I had to find a way to protect myself from these bots. That's when I started using zip bombs.
A zip bomb is a relatively small compressed file that can expand into a very large file that can overwhelm a machine.
A feature that was developed early on the web was compression with gzip. The Internet being slow and information being dense, the idea was to compress data as small as possible before transmitting it through the wire. So an 50 KB HTML file, composed of text, can be compressed to 10K, thus saving you 40KB in transmission. On dial up Internet, this meant downloading the page in 3 seconds instead of 12 seconds.
This same compression can be used to serve CSS, Javascript, or even images. Gzip is fast, simple and drastically improves the browsing experience. When a browser makes a web request, it includes the headers that signals the target server that it can support compression. And if the server also supports it, it will return a compressed version of the expected data.
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate
Bots that crawl the web also support this feature. Especially since their job is to ingest data from all over the web, they maximize their bandwidth by using compression. And we can take full advantage of this feature.
On this blog, I often get bots that scan for security vulnerabilities, which I ignore for the most part. But when I detect that they are either trying to inject malicious attacks, or are probing for a response, I return a 200 OK response, and serve them a gzip response. I vary from a 1MB to 10MB file which they are happy to ingest. For the most part, when they do, I never hear from them again. Why? Well, that's because they crash right after ingesting the file.
Content-Encoding: deflate, gzip
What happens is, they receive the file, read the header that instructs them that it is a compressed file. So they try to decompress the 1MB file to find whatever content they are looking for. But the file expands, and expands, and expands, until they run out of memory and their server crashes. The 1MB file decompresses into a 1GB. This is more than enough to break most bots. However, for those pesky scripts that won't stop, I serve them the 10MB file. This one decompresses into 10GB and instantly kills the script.
Before I tell you how to create a zip bomb, I do have to warn you that you can potentially crash and destroy your own device. Continue at your own risk. So here is how we create the zip bomb:
dd if=/dev/zero bs=1G count=10 | gzip -c > 10GB.gz
Here is what the command does:
dd
: The dd command is used to copy or convert data.
if
: Input file, specifies
/dev/zero
a special file that produces an infinite stream of zero bytes.
bs
: block size, sets the block size to 1 gigabyte (1G), meaning dd will read and write data in chunks of 1 GB at a time.
count=10
: This tells dd to process 10 blocks, each 1 GB in size. So, this will generate 10 GB of zeroed data.
We then pass the output of the command to gzip which will compress the output into the file 10GB.gz. The resulting file is 10MB in this case.
On my server, I've added a middleware that checks if the current request is malicious or not. I have a list of black-listed ips that try to scan the whole website repeatedly. I have other heuristics in place to detect spammers. A lot of spammers attempt to spam a page, then come back to see if the spam has made it to the page. I use this pattern to detect them. It looks something like this:
if (ipIsBlackListed() || isMalicious()) {
header("Content-Encoding: deflate, gzip");
header("Content-Length: "+ filesize(ZIP_BOMB_FILE_10G)); // 10 MB
readfile(ZIP_BOMB_FILE_10G);
exit;
}
That's all it takes. The only price I pay is that I'm serving a 10MB file now on some occasions. If I have an article going viral, I decrease it to the 1MB file, which is just as effective.
One more thing, a zip bomb is not foolproof. It can be easily detected and circumvented. You could partially read the content after all. But for unsophisticated bots that are blindly crawling the web disrupting servers, this is a good enough tool for protecting your server.
You can see it in action in

data.article_summary: 《Can we make gamepad typing fast?》一文介绍了Rad Type，一种专为游戏手柄设计的新型键盘，旨在提升游戏手柄文字输入速度。尽管游戏手柄已有四十多年历史，但文字输入方式改进有限。Rad Type通过将字母排列在两个同心圆上，用户通过移动摇杆选择字母，输入速度远超传统QWERTY键盘。文章还介绍了Rad Type的演变过程，从最初的“时钟”设计到增加外围大圈以提高精确度的第二版，以及后续的改进版本。该设计不仅适用于游戏手柄，也为触屏和传统键盘提供了一种有趣的替代方案。文章最后探讨了设计背后的动机，包括在《Forza Motorsport 7》和《Rec Room》中的应用需求。

• **tmtvl**：建议基于Dvorak或Workman键盘布局，而非传统的QWERTY布局，以提高输入效率。他还提出了使用D-Pad和多键盘切换的具体方案，并提到数字和特殊字符的安排。

• **pests**：抱怨了某些流媒体应用中的输入延迟问题，指出快速移动光标时会产生输入滞后，导致输入错误。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对输入速度和准确性的关注点不同，有人关注硬件设备的识别速度，有人关注键盘布局的优化。
• 讨论中提到了多个类似系统和插件，如YouTube的PS4输入法、《魔兽世界》的consoleport插件和Nokia 3600/3650的输入法。

Rad Type
2025-04-28
Can we make gamepad typing fast?
Gamepad text input is fascinating. It's been over 40 years since the NES launched, yet we've seen little improvement beyond selecting characters from a QWERTY keyboard with directional input. This page introduces Rad Type: a new kind of gamepad keyboard with a hardware-centric design. Despite the brand new UX, I'd wager that most users can pick it up immediately and type many times faster than any other gamepad keyboard interface.
Housekeeping
If you're using a gamepad, click this toggle to configure your input settings. A sensible default is provided, so you can skip configuration and come back if things don't work as expected. If you're on touch or keyboard + mouse, you can ignore these settings--parity controls are available to simulate thumbstick input. While Rad Type is designed with gamepads in mind, it also offers an interesting alternative to the traditional QWERTY touch keyboard. Touch users my want to experiment with both portrait and landscape orientations.

What is Rad Type?
Rad Type features two circles with alphabet characters arranged in rings. To enter a character, move the thumbstick in its direction and release. A character is input when the target dot moves from the outer ring to the middle ring. For center characters, press the thumbstick inward. Space and Delete are usually mapped to gamepad buttons like X and A. I recommend using the left button on your gamepad for Delete and the bottom button for Space.
If you're using a gamepad, make sure the "Target with Gamepad" toggle is enabled. This page explores multiple Rad Type examples, and the toggle determines which one is active. On touch or mouse + keyboard, you can simulate thumbstick input by tapping-and-draggging or clicking-and-dragging. You can also tap or click individual letters or buttons directly.

Hello my name is

The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog

You'll find more Rad Type variants further down in this post. But first, lets discuss some of the motivation behind Rad Type.
Motivation
I came up with the idea for Rad Type while working on Car Select for
Forza Motorsport 7
. With over 700 cars, browsing was tedious. You flipped through makes using the gamepad bumpers and models using the thumbsticks, and it could take awhile to find the car you wanted. I wanted a fuzzy search interface to speed things up, but gamepad input would make that feel like a downgrade.
We never implemented fuzzy search in
Forza 7
, but I later had the chance to build it into
Rec Room
's palette.
Rec Room
features a huge library of objects, shapes, and programming elements that Creators use to build games. We needed a way for Creators to quickly search through it all. Our first version of fuzzy search was based on
Anders Elfgren's Medium post
.
Rec Room
runs on multiple platforms and Palette Search works great on most of them--but gamepads still struggle.
Version 1: Clocks
While thinking about ways to improve gamepad input, I pictured a clock face--its 12 numbers arranged around its hands. I thought, "12 times 2 is 24, and there's only 26 letters in the alphabet." The last two letters fell into place in the center of the clock when I remembered that most thumbsticks also clicked like buttons. That's how the first version of Rad Type was born:

Version 2: Precision
The first version of Rad Type works, but its easy to enter the wrong character as the targeting dot snaps back to center. In the small circle, even slight thumb imprecision has a big impact. the second version of Rad Type adds a larger ring near the the perimiter. With more room to move before entering a character, the dot now absorbs small inaccuracies with less impact to character selection.

• **pests**：抱怨了某些流媒体应用中的输入延迟问题，指出快速移动光标时会产生输入滞后，导致输入错误。
• **madmod**：提到了PSP上类似的自制输入法，指出使用摇杆进行输入的设计早已有之。
• **spongebobstoes**：提到《魔兽世界》的consoleport插件中已有类似的输入方法，并提供了一个演示动画链接。
• **re**：认为当前设计虽然受QWERTY启发，但建议D和V键应互换以更符合QWERTY布局，并质疑是否测试过其他排列方式。
• **CasperH2O**：表示有兴趣将这种输入法集成到开源应用Handheld Companion中。
• **svarrall**：希望看到不同输入变体的速度和准确性对比数据，并提到Nokia 3600/3650的径向按钮布局与此类似。
• **MetaMonk**：指出这种输入法可能借鉴了Perlin的实验页面，提到了Quikwriting输入法。
• **catapart**：喜欢这种输入方式，但建议将删除键移到右圆180度位置，并在原位置放置第二个空格键。
• **socalgal2**：询问如何输入非ASCII字符或带重音的字符。
• **tyleo**：认为这种径向输入法在手机触摸屏上也有优势，因为拇指到每个字符的距离相等。
• **0cf8612b2e1e**：询问这种输入法是否曾在Steam控制器上出现过。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对输入速度和准确性的关注点不同，有人关注硬件设备的识别速度，有人关注键盘布局的优化。
• 讨论中提到了多个类似系统和插件，如YouTube的PS4输入法、《魔兽世界》的consoleport插件和Nokia 3600/3650的输入法。
• 多个用户提出了具体的改进建议，如stolksdorf的摇杆和肩键功能分配、catapart的按键位置调整等。
• 争议的焦点主要在于哪种键盘布局（QWERTY、Dvorak、Workman或其他）能提供最佳的输入效率，以及如何处理特殊字符的输入问题。

主要讨论点：不同形式的过去文化记录的真实性和价值

不同观点：
• [alganet] 认为过去文化的记录存在多种形式，包括电影、歌曲等文化产物，而不仅仅是新闻或报纸。他们内部曾有争论，部分人认为文化产物更能代表历史，而另一些人则坚持新闻等传统媒介更准确。经过一段时间，他们成功整合了多种视角，但后来因一些统计异常和信息噪音，他们重新筛选并确认了可信来源，最终成功还原了历史。这一过程虽然艰难，但最终恢复了跨时间的沟通和文化传承。

• [Mistletoe] 提供了一个现代生活中的例子，指出像Taylor Swift这样的明星及其粉丝文化对某些年轻人生活的影响，尤其是他们缺乏实际人际关系，更多地沉浸在明星的寄生消费中。这种生活方式被认为是怪异的，因为这些人更多地关注明星的琐事，而非建立真实的人际关系。

• [smitty1e] 分享了一个关于寻找失落的音乐作品的故事，强调了互联网文化中对丢失媒体的执着追寻和最终发现的喜悦。这个例子展示了人们如何在现代通过集体努力还原和庆祝过去的文化产物，类似于[alganet]所描述的历史还原过程。

• 争议的焦点在于过去文化的记录和还原方法。一方面是电影、歌曲等文化产物是否能准确代表历史，另一方面是新闻和报纸等传统媒介的可靠性。

• [alganet]的经验显示了多视角方法的成功，但也指出了信息噪音和虚假信息的问题，这需要通过统计异常和可信来源的筛选来解决。

• [Mistletoe]的例子揭示了现代社会中粉丝文化对个人生活的影响，特别是寄生消费现象带来的实际人际关系缺失问题。

• [smitty1e]的例子展示了互联网文化中对丢失媒体的追寻和发现过程，这与[alganet]的历史还原过程有相似之处，强调了集体努力和信息共享的重要性。

data.title: Duolingo will replace contract workers with AI
data.author: donohoe
data.article_summary: Duolingo CEO Luis von Ahn宣布公司将转向“AI优先”战略，逐渐停止使用承包商来完成AI能处理的工作。这一转变旨在通过AI消除瓶颈，让员工专注于创造性和更具挑战性的任务，而非重复性工作。公司计划在招聘和绩效评估中纳入AI使用情况的考量，且只有在团队无法进一步自动化工作时才会增加人手。Von Ahn强调，此举并非用AI取代员工，而是为了更好地实现公司的教学使命，迅速为学习者提供大量内容。同时，公司会提供培训和工具支持员工适应这一变化。这一决策受到Shopify CEO类似措施的启发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Duolingo的“AI优先”政策及其影响

不同观点：
• **对工程师工作影响的担忧**：Aurornis指出，Duolingo的内部公告暗示编码将变得不再重要，生产力预期却要提高，这令人担忧。强制要求开发人员在每个任务中使用AI，并通过大语言模型（LLM）来工作，而不是直接写代码，这种做法可能源于对LLM理解有限的非开发人员。Aurornis认为，这种做法不会显著提高生产力，反而可能适得其反。

• **Duolingo产品有效性的质疑**：n_ary和Larrikin认为Duolingo作为一个语言学习工具并不有效，它只是提供了一些基础的学习内容，类似于Anki这样的闪卡工具，但学习效果不佳。n_ary决定支持“以人为本”的企业，报名参加真实的语言课程。Larrikin则指出，Duolingo的内容过于基础，无法帮助学习者真正掌握一门语言。

• **对AI内容生成需求的质疑**：actuallyalys和SirensOfTitan质疑Duolingo声称的需要大量AI生成内容的理由。他们认为，创建学习材料主要是一个前期的任务，后续只需要少量更新和修正，不需要如此大规模地依赖AI。SirensOfTitan进一步指出，如果AI工具真的能显著提高生产力，就不需要强制推行。

• **对Duolingo未来发展的悲观预测**：iamleppert和boh对Duolingo的未来表示悲观。iamleppert预测Duolingo可能在18个月内消失，而boh认为“AI优先”只是掩盖 struggling business 的策略，实际上是通过削减人力成本来伪装成创新。

• **对AI在语言学习中作用的质疑**：nope1000和qalmakka指出，LLM在语言学习中的应用存在问题。由于LLM给出的答案可能看似正确但实际上错误，学习者无法验证其准确性。qalmakka进一步认为，AI应该作为人类的辅助工具，而不是取代人类技能，管理层对AI的理解不足，导致错误地将其视为可以完全取代人类劳动的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• **AI技术与传统方法的比较**：spunker540认为，尽管Duolingo目前受到批评，但未来新的AI辅导应用可能会超越它，就像Duolingo曾经超越CD和书籍一样。

• **Duolingo初衷的背离**：gs17通过引用Luis Von Ahn的初衷，指出Duolingo已经偏离了其最初提供高质量免费语言教育的使命。

• **Duolingo作为时间消耗品**：klipklop和xdfgh1112认为，Duolingo对大多数人来说并没有实际效果，只是一个浪费时间的应用。

• **相关替代方案的提及**：dang提到了一个开源的Duolingo替代品LibreLingo，供用户选择。

News
Duolingo will replace contract workers with AI
The company is going to be ‘AI-first,’ says its CEO.
The company is going to be ‘AI-first,’ says its CEO.
by
Jay Peters
Apr 28, 2025, 11:47 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Duolingo co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn.
Photo: Getty Images
Jay Peters
is a news editor covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.
Duolingo will “gradually stop using contractors to do work that AI can handle,” according to an all-hands email sent by co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn announcing that the company will be “AI-first.” The email was posted on
Duolingo’s LinkedIn account
.
According to von Ahn, being “AI-first” means the company will “need to rethink much of how we work” and that “making minor tweaks to systems designed for humans won’t get us there.” As part of the shift, the company will roll out “a few constructive constraints,” including the changes to how it works with contractors, looking for AI use in hiring and in performance reviews, and that “headcount will only be given if a team cannot automate more of their work.”
von Ahn says that “Duolingo will remain a company that cares deeply about its employees” and that “this isn’t about replacing Duos with AI.” Instead, he says that the changes are “about removing bottlenecks” so that employees can “focus on creative work and real problems, not repetitive tasks.”
Related
Shopify CEO says no new hires without proof AI can’t do the job
“AI isn’t just a productivity boost,” von Ahn says. “It helps us get closer to our mission. To teach well, we need to create a massive amount of content, and doing that manually doesn’t scale. One of the best decisions we made recently was replacing a slow, manual content creation process with one powered by AI. Without AI, it would take us decades to scale our content to more learners. We owe it to our learners to get them this content ASAP.”
von Ahn’s email follows a similar memo Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke sent to employees and recently
shared online
. In that memo, Lütke said that before teams asked for more headcount or resources, they needed to show “why they cannot get what they want done using AI.”
Here’s the text of von Ahn’s memo from Duolingo’s LinkedIn post:
I’ve said this in Q&As and many meetings, but I want to make it official:
Duolingo is going to be AI-first
.
AI is already changing how work gets done. It’s not a question of if or when. It’s happening now. When there’s a shift this big, the worst thing you can do is wait. In 2012, we bet on mobile. While others were focused on mobile companion apps for websites, we decided to build mobile-first because we saw it was the future. That decision helped us win the 2013 iPhone App of the Year and unlocked the organic word-of-mouth growth that followed.
Betting on mobile made all the difference. We’re making a similar call now, and this time the platform shift is AI.
AI isn’t just a productivity boost
. It helps us get closer to our mission. To teach well, we need to create a massive amount of content, and doing that manually doesn’t scale. One of the best decisions we made recently was replacing a slow, manual content creation process with one powered by AI. Without AI, it would take us decades to scale our content to more learners. We owe it to our learners to get them this content ASAP.
AI also helps us build features like Video Call that were impossible to build before.
For the first time ever, teaching as well as the best human tutors is within our reach.
Being AI-first means we will need to rethink much of how we work.
Making minor tweaks to systems designed for humans won’t get us there
. In many cases, we’ll need to start from scratch. We’re not going to rebuild everything overnight, and some things-like getting AI to understand our codebase-will take time. However, we can’t wait until the technology is 100% perfect. We’d rather move with urgency and take occasional small hits on quality than move slowly and miss the moment.
We’ll be rolling out a few constructive constraints to help guide this shift:
We’ll gradually stop using contractors to do work that AI can handle
AI use will be part of what we look for in hiring
AI use will be part of what we evaluate in performance reviews
Headcount will only be given if a team cannot automate more of their work
Most functions will have specific initiatives to fundamentally change how they work
All of this said,
Duolingo will remain a company that cares deeply about its employees
. This isn’t about replacing Duos with AI. It’s about removing bottlenecks so we can do more with the outstanding Duos we already have. We want you to focus on creative work and real problems, not repetitive tasks.
We’re going to support you with more training, mentorship, and tooling for AI in your function.
Change can be scary, but I’m confident this will be a great step for Duolingo. It will help us better deliver on our mission — and for Duos, it means st

data.title: Show HN: A Common Lisp implementation in development, supports ASDF
data.author: andreamonaco
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为"alisp"的Lisp实现项目，该项目目前处于Beta阶段，目标是实现Common Lisp的大部分功能，但并非严格遵循。项目使用C89编写，依赖GNU readline和GNU mp库，提供解释器以及一些开发工具如分析器和调试器。项目定期更新，已发布多个版本，最新版本为1.1，增加了对LOOP、编译器、文件系统支持和多种错误修复的改进。alisp以GPLv3或更高版本发布，欢迎提交错误报告和建议，但暂不接受补丁。项目主页提供了源码下载和捐赠链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个新Lisp语言项目的技术决策、托管平台选择、许可证问题及其未来发展方向

不同观点：
• 关于技术优先级的选择：[nexo-v1] 好奇为什么项目早期优先实现 stepping（单步调试）和 watchpoints（观察点），是为了调试编译器代码还是为了满足终端用户的需求。这表明对项目早期开发重点的关注，并隐含了关于调试功能重要性的不同潜在理由。

• 关于项目托管平台的选择：[danilor] 对项目托管在 nongnu 而非 GitHub/GitLab 表示好奇，反映了对自由软件托管平台的兴趣和了解不足，暗示了主流平台（如GitHub）与非主流平台（nongnu）之间的选择问题。

• 关于项目目标和未来发展：[badmonster] 询问项目是否计划支持全 native code 编译，还是仅作为解释器存在，这关系到项目的长期技术路线和功能规划。[neonscribe] 则直接询问项目的目标，反映出对项目愿景的兴趣。

• 关于许可证问题：[valorzard] 提出对 GPLv3 许可证的担忧，认为它限制了项目在某些项目中的使用，建议是否可能更改为 LGPL 或 MPL，这涉及到开源许可证的选择及其对项目采用率的影响。

补充讨论：
• 关于 CL（Common Lisp）实现的库兼容性和社区需求：[whartung] 提到 CL 实现需要多少库代码才能开始利用现有库（在许可允许的情况下），特别是关于 LOOP 宏和运行时的可移植性问题，暗示对社区资源共享和避免重复劳动的关注。
